title: Gochujang Chicken Thighs
summary: Sticky, smoky-sweet pan-seared chicken thighs in a gochujang marinade. A weeknight Korean home-cooking staple that forgives beginners and rewards a hot pan.

ingredients.name: gochujang
ingredients.notes: Korean red chili paste; heat varies by brand

steps.instruction: Make the marinade: in a large bowl, whisk together the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and rice vinegar until smooth.
success_cues: Marinade is glossy and uniform with no streaks of honey or paste

steps.instruction: Add the chicken pieces to the bowl and toss until every piece is coated. Cover and let it sit for 20 minutes at room temperature, or refrigerate up to overnight.
success_cues: Every piece is evenly red with no bare patches
warnings: Raw poultry: wash your hands, the board and any utensils with hot soapy water after handling. Keep the marinated chicken away from ready-to-eat food.
steps.creator_note: I mix this in the morning and let it marinate all day in the fridge; the ginger and garlic go much deeper.

steps.instruction: Heat a large, heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Add the neutral oil and wait until it shimmers.
success_cues: Oil shimmers and a drop of marinade sizzles the moment it hits the pan

steps.instruction: Lay the chicken in a single layer, leaving space between pieces, and let it cook undisturbed for 4 to 5 minutes. Work in two batches if the pan is crowded.
success_cues: Deep mahogany crust on the first side
Pieces release from the pan without tugging
warnings: The honey and gochujang burn fast: if the pan smokes heavily, lower the heat rather than pushing through.

steps.instruction: Flip each piece and cook 5 to 6 minutes more, spooning any marinade left in the bowl over the chicken so it reduces into a glaze.
success_cues: Glaze thickens and clings to the chicken
An instant-read thermometer reads 165°F (74°C) in the thickest piece
warnings: Chicken is done only when an instant-read thermometer reads 165°F (74°C) in the thickest piece. Do not judge doneness by color alone.

steps.instruction: Take the pan off the heat and let the chicken rest in the pan juices for 3 minutes, tossing once so the glaze coats every piece.
success_cues: Juices settle and the glaze looks sticky rather than runny

steps.instruction: Serve over rice, topped with the sliced scallions and sesame seeds.
success_cues: Scallions stay bright green and crisp on top

creator_notes: Boneless thighs forgive an extra minute of cooking far better than breasts do; use thighs the first time you make this.
Gochujang brands vary a lot in heat. Start with 2 tablespoons if you are unsure and add more to the marinade next time.
dietary_warnings: Most gochujang and soy sauce contain wheat; check labels if avoiding gluten.
